Abstract

With the rapid development of electronic industry, it's pressing to develop multifunctional electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding materials to ensure the stable operation of electronic devices. Herein, multilayered flexible PEG@PAN/MXene (Ti3C2Tx)/PVDF@SiO2 (PMF) composite film has been constructed from the level of microstructure design via coaxial electrospinning, coating spraying, and uniaxial electrospinning strategies. Benefiting from the effective encapsulation for PEG and high conductivity of MXene coating, PEG@PAN/MXene composite film with MXene coating loading density of 0.70 mg cm−2 exhibits high thermal energy storage density of 120.77 J g−1 and great EMI shielding performance (EMI SE of 34.409 dB and SSE of 49.086 dB cm3 g−1) in X-band (8–12 GHz). Therefore, this advanced composite film can not only help electronic devices prevent the influence of electromagnetic pollution in the X-band but also play an important role in electronic device thermal management. Additionally, the deposition of nano PVDF@SiO2 fibers (289 ± 128 nm) endowed the PMF composite film with great hydrophobic properties (water contact angle of 126.5°) to ensure the stable working of hydrophilic MXene coating, thereby breaks the limitation of humid application environments. The finding paves a new way for the development of novel multifunctional EMI shielding composite films for electronic devices.

1 Introduction

Nowadays, the emergence and development of electronic science and information technology have brought a profound impact on the production and lifestyles of human society.[1, 2] And the most representative phenomenon is that humans are inseparable from various electronic devices, which absolutely improve their life quality.[3] However, exposure of human to electromagnetic radiation emitted from these electronic devices has increased dramatically, which causes chronic health problems, such as fatigue, headache, and cancer. And electromagnetic pollution would cause bad effect to precision instruments, wireless equipment, national defense military equipment, etc.[4] In this regard, electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding and microwave-absorbing materials can be used to solve the urgent problem.[5, 6] Meanwhile, the miniaturization and integration of electronic devices have brought about the heat dissipation problem, which seriously affects the normal operation of equipment and accelerates device aging.[7] Therefore, it's an urgent task to develop advanced composite materials with EMI shielding performance and effective thermal management properties in this era.[8, 9]

In this work, novel multilayered PEG@PAN/MXene/PVDF@SiO2 (PMF) composite film with waterproof property was designed for effective EMI shielding and thermal management application of electronic devices via a simple coaxial electrospinning technology, double-side spraying strategy, and uniaxial electrospinning method. As shown in Figure 1, there exist several advantages for this advanced composite film: 1) The core-shell microstructure achieves the effective encapsulation of PEG to solve the leakage problem during working, shape instability and fragility, which endows the flexible PEG@PAN film with high energy storage density of 133.77 J g−1 and excellent thermal reliability that endured 300 thermal cycles. 2) Thin and flexible PEG@PAN/MXene (PM) composite film, possessing EMI shielding performance in X-band and thermal management function, was provided via simple double-side spraying strategy, which can simultaneously remove two major application obstacles of electronic devices. 3) The introduction of a hydrophobic PVDF@SiO2 fiber layer on PM film constructs a protective barrier for the normal working of MXene, which breaks the limitation of the application environment. 4) The film has also gained enhanced thermal conductivity which is beneficial for the thermal management of electronic devices. Finally, the EMI shielding mechanism, thermal management working mechanism, and the effect mechanism of SiO2’s content on hydrophobic properties were also explored in detail.
